[2/8/24, 6:27:47 PM] Grandma Miller: How's the hospital experience going, Chloe
[2/9/24, 7:53:19 PM] Chloe: It’s been interesting lol. I’m not sure exactly what mom already told you so some of this might be repeatitive.  

The first thing is that medical students have a very different role here because students basically only shadow and do not do the things we do in the US (talk to patients alone, help with sutures, assist in procedure/surgery, etc.). They also have a different viewpoint on attendance, which is that “we are not paying you to be here, so it’s up to you what time/how much time you want to spend here”. Whereas at home we have very strict schedules and attendance policies. So adjusting to that cultural difference has been kinda challenging because it feels so different that what I’m used to!
[2/9/24, 7:54:24 PM] Grandma Miller: Are you bored not getting to do anything
[2/9/24, 7:54:39 PM] Aunt Karen: Sounds like a great opportunity to see what Ireland has to offer outside the hospital!
[2/9/24, 7:55:11 PM] Chloe: The ER here is also much less effecient. Yesterday when I was shadowing one of the senior house officers (their term for a resident the year after their intern year) it took her like 2 hours just to work on one patient because all of the systems were so inefficient. Like rather than being able to page the surgeons to come see the patient and then move onto the next one, they had to keep calling the surgeons until they answered and it took about an hour and a half to get ahold of anyone!
[2/9/24, 7:55:55 PM] Aunt Karen: 😲
[2/9/24, 7:55:56 PM] Chloe: They have also had a major hospital system go down almost everyday! Yesterday the imaging viewing system for X-rays and other scans went down for 2 hours so they could not view any of those scans at all!
[2/9/24, 7:55:56 PM] Grandma Miller: Oh gosh l..not a good system
[2/9/24, 7:56:11 PM] Chloe: And one day the lab went down, so they were not able to run any lab tests for several hours
[2/9/24, 7:56:17 PM] Grandma Miller: Yikes!
[2/9/24, 7:56:24 PM] Chloe: Yes it’s concerning!
[2/9/24, 7:56:30 PM] Aunt Karen: Wow! Makes you appreciate even the most inefficient system here!
[2/9/24, 7:56:56 PM] Grandma Miller: Wouldn't want you experience that as a sick patient
[2/9/24, 7:57:23 PM] Chloe: One day a patient needed an urgent ultrasound to rule out a DVT so they had to send the patient upstairs for the US. And rather than the doctors receiving the US results directly, the US people just gave a paper with the results to the patient. And then eventually the patient saw the doctor walking by again and was like- hey I have my US results!
[2/9/24, 7:57:50 PM] Grandma Miller: Oh my gosh
[2/9/24, 7:57:52 PM] Chloe: But like if the patient had lost the paper or not given it to the doctor then they would not have ever seen the results because it’s all a paper system
[2/9/24, 7:58:13 PM] Chloe: And it is kinda boring not being able to do anything
[2/9/24, 7:58:23 PM] Aunt Karen: I went to an outpatient appointment today, and they ordered an xray, did it, read it, gave me an injection, and ordered PT - and the results and the note hit my patient portal before I left the parking lot!
[2/9/24, 7:58:35 PM] Chloe: Wow that’s fast!
[2/9/24, 7:58:49 PM] Grandma Miller: Sounds terrible...nothing like the US
[2/9/24, 7:59:35 PM] Grandma Miller: Well at least you are really getting time to experience Ireland
[2/9/24, 7:59:53 PM] Chloe: But yes here it’s mainly paper! They have all sorts of systems to juggle tho. They write all of their clinic notes on paper, but in the ER the notes are online. They have to open multiple seperate windows to order scans, a different one for labs. Have to just call consults until they answer. Do not have a paging system. And to order medications they just write it on a sheet that sits by the patients bed that the nurse will occasionally come look at
[2/9/24, 8:00:13 PM] Aunt Karen: The nurse for my appointment has a friend in med school at Pine Valley who's wanting to do a rotation in Italy, but she's worried about the cost
[2/9/24, 8:00:24 PM] Chloe: I will definitely appreciate all of the systems that we have in the US for sure after this!
[2/9/24, 8:00:44 PM] Aunt Karen: 💯
[2/9/24, 8:01:00 PM] Chloe: That makes sense! It was definitely costly for us to come here! It’s very interesting to see how different the system is!
[2/9/24, 8:02:13 PM] Aunt Karen: What happens if there's a trauma? Do they have access to records?
[2/9/24, 8:02:20 PM] Chloe: My friend Emily Carter (Aunt Karen is friends with her aunt) is here too but she is rotating in psychiatry. It’s interesting to hear her experience too because the mental health care here seems much better than in the US because it is much more accessible. In the US a lot of mental health care is not covrrrd by insurance but here they have a public system and it covers all of the mental health things
[2/9/24, 8:02:44 PM] Chloe: They only have access to records of them being in that specific ER. Despite it being a public system they don’t have records that span multiple hospitals
[2/9/24, 8:03:07 PM] Grandma Miller: That's really interesting  about mental health
[2/9/24, 8:03:14 PM] Chloe: And they don’t have records of if they were an inpatient in that hospital always unless it was uploaded from the paper chart to the computer one
[2/9/24, 8:03:29 PM] Aunt Karen: Oh, wow
[2/9/24, 8:04:30 PM] Chloe: Another big difference here is the attendings (they call them consultants) don’t have to see all of the patients that the residents see. The residents just ask for help if they think they need it but they aren’t necessarily required to have an attending lay eyes on the patient and sign off on their decision making
[2/9/24, 8:05:02 PM] Grandma Miller: Oh boy. Scary!
[2/9/24, 8:05:11 PM] Chloe: Yes it’s a bit concerning!
[2/9/24, 8:05:38 PM] Aunt Karen: Even first-year residents? I hope I don't have a medical problem in Ireland someday
[2/9/24, 8:07:03 PM] Chloe: Yes even the interns don’t seem to be really checking in with the consultants. I think they do at some point, but it’s not necessarily during the care of the patient. After they discharge they might reveiw it, and I have heard them calling patients several times to tell them that they missed something… 😬 It seems like the consultants are somewhat trying to check in with the interns but that the system is not in place to do that so it doesn’t always happen especially when things get busy (which seems to be often)
[2/9/24, 8:07:24 PM] Chloe: I don’t necessarily feel confident about going to this ER as a patient lol
[2/9/24, 8:07:35 PM] Aunt Karen: Is there a physician shortage in Ireland?
[2/9/24, 8:07:41 PM] Chloe: I think they also have private ERs for people who have private  health insurance
[2/9/24, 8:07:50 PM] Chloe: The one I am at is a public one
[2/9/24, 8:07:54 PM] Grandma Miller: Hope you don't have to
[2/9/24, 8:07:58 PM] Chloe: Im not sure!
[2/9/24, 8:08:22 PM] Aunt Karen: I know there is in England (shortage)
[2/9/24, 8:09:33 PM] Chloe: I wouldn’t be surprised if there was. However also they would be able to have each doctor see WAY more patients if they fixed some of their efficiency and system issues. Because while I’ve been there during the day there have been at least 15 doctors on shift which is a lot for the size of the ER but it takes so long to do all of the things they need to do that it seems to take forever to see the patients
[2/9/24, 8:10:17 PM] Grandma Miller: Crazy it's that inefficient
[2/9/24, 8:10:33 PM] Chloe: There are some good differences as well too. For example the patients here are much more appreciative of the care and respectful towards the doctors.
[2/9/24, 8:10:52 PM] Grandma Miller: Interesting
[2/9/24, 8:11:11 PM] Chloe: In the US it’s pretty common to hear patients in the ER yelling at the doctors/nurses, walking around naked, threatening to pee on people, or acting violent. I haven’t seen anything remotely like that here
[2/9/24, 8:11:48 PM] Grandma Miller: Ok.  Well that's crazy too.
[2/9/24, 8:11:57 PM] Chloe: One day one patient was mildly cussing at them, and they told the patient that they could leave and come back when they were able to act appropriately. Which even these horrible patients in the US I have never seen any of them asked to leave 😂 they just get a security guard in their room haha
[2/9/24, 8:12:28 PM] Chloe: They also don’t have any security guards in the ER here which is super different. But it seems like they really don’t need them.
[2/9/24, 8:12:54 PM] Chloe: Emily also said that the impatient psych units are not locked here! Even for the involuntary patients! But the patients just stay anyway
[2/9/24, 8:12:58 PM] Grandma Miller: You could write a thesis on this
[2/9/24, 8:13:21 PM] Chloe: I do have a lot of random observations lol
[2/9/24, 8:13:36 PM] Grandma Miller: Oh my gosh
[2/9/24, 8:13:44 PM] Aunt Karen: Quite a testament to the clichéd "ugly American"
[2/9/24, 8:14:09 PM] Aunt Karen: That's worth studying
[2/9/24, 8:14:45 PM] Chloe: Yes it’s super interesting!
[2/9/24, 8:14:55 PM] Grandma Miller: People here have no idea how lucky we are
[2/9/24, 8:15:31 PM] Chloe: It’s also interesting because from the Psych perspective Emily is seeing a really positive impact of having a public health care system. But then from the ED perspective it seems more negative because it feels downright unsafe.
[2/9/24, 8:16:02 PM] Chloe: I’m definitely going to appreciate things a lot more when I go back for sure!
[2/9/24, 8:16:10 PM] Aunt Karen: Lots to learn from both perspectives
[2/9/24, 8:16:11 PM] Grandma Miller: What does,Sullivan say about his department
[2/9/24, 8:16:26 PM] Chloe: He is not as talkative as Emily so he hasn’t shared as many stories haha.
[2/9/24, 8:16:46 PM] Grandma Miller: You'll have to ask him his impressions
[2/9/24, 8:16:59 PM] Chloe: He says one big difference is that only the people operating in the OR wear masks, but the students and other people standing around the side a few feet from the patient do not wear masks
[2/9/24, 8:17:03 PM] Chloe: He is doing Urologu
[2/9/24, 8:17:09 PM] Chloe: Urology
[2/9/24, 8:17:14 PM] Aunt Karen: Omg!
[2/9/24, 8:17:33 PM] Chloe: Yes we were all suprised!
[2/9/24, 8:18:08 PM] Chloe: I was also shocked to see that they don’t wash out wounds in the ER here before they suture them! They just sew them up! In the US we use a few full bottles of saline even on small cuts!
[2/9/24, 8:18:29 PM] Grandma Miller: Oh good grief. Yikes
[2/9/24, 8:18:52 PM] Aunt Karen: 😱😱😱
[2/9/24, 8:19:08 PM] Grandma Miller: Doesn't sound like very good infection control not wearing masks
[2/9/24, 8:19:31 PM] Chloe: Ya… it’s interesting. I wonder if they have had problems with it or if what we are doing is just overkill?
[2/9/24, 8:19:56 PM] Grandma Miller: A study would be interesting
[2/9/24, 8:19:59 PM] Chloe: But I do feel like the cleanliness standards for the hospital are lower here, at least in the ER
[2/9/24, 8:20:15 PM] Chloe: I will have to look up and see if anyone has done any research studies on some of these things
